legend: Rudolf has prepared a set of n%%ZSMJ0%% problems with complexities a1<a2<a3<⋯<an%%ZSMJ1%%. He is not entirely satisfied with the balance, so he wants to add at most one problem to fix it.

For this, Rudolf came up with m%%ZSMJ2%% models of problems and k%%ZSMJ3%% functions. The complexity of the i%%ZSMJ4%%-th model is di%%ZSMJ5%%, and the complexity of the j%%ZSMJ6%%-th function is fj%%ZSMJ7%%. To create a problem, he selects values i%%ZSMJ8%% and j%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤i≤m%%ZSMJ10%%, 1≤j≤k%%ZSMJ11%%) and by combining the i%%ZSMJ12%%-th model with the j%%ZSMJ13%%-th function, he obtains a new problem with complexity di+fj%%ZSMJ14%% (a new element is inserted into the array a%%ZSMJ15%%).
To determine the imbalance of the set, Rudolf sorts the complexities of the problems in ascending order and finds the largest value of ai−ai−1%%ZSMJ16%% (i>1%%ZSMJ17%%).
What is the minimum value of imbalance that Rudolf can achieve by adding at most one problem, created according to the described rules?
input: The first line of the input contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ18%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ19%%) — the number of testcases.

The first line of each test case contains three integers n%%ZSMJ20%%, m%%ZSMJ21%%, and k%%ZSMJ22%% (2≤n≤105%%ZSMJ23%%, 1≤m,k≤2⋅105%%ZSMJ24%%) — the number of prepared problems, the number of models, and the number of functions, respectively.
The second line of each test case contains n%%ZSMJ25%% integers a1,a2,a3,…an%%ZSMJ26%% (1≤ai≤2⋅109%%ZSMJ27%%, ai<ai+1%%ZSMJ28%%) — the complexities of the prepared problems.
The third line of each test case contains m%%ZSMJ29%% integers d1,d2,d3,…dm%%ZSMJ30%% (1≤di≤109%%ZSMJ31%%) — the complexities of the models.
The fourth line of each test case contains k%%ZSMJ32%% integers f1,f2,f3,…fk%%ZSMJ33%% (1≤fi≤109%%ZSMJ34%%) — the complexities of the functions.
It is guaranteed that the sum of n%%ZSMJ35%% over all testcases does not exceed 105%%ZSMJ36%%.
It is guaranteed that the sum of m%%ZSMJ37%% over all testcases does not exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ38%%.
It is guaranteed that the sum of k%%ZSMJ39%% over all testcases does not exceed 2⋅105%%ZSMJ40%%.
output: For each testcase, output a single number — the minimum imbalance that Rudolf can achieve.
